bill-cooper.text: Voted yes (April 1, 2025) on Resolution SCV-469, adopting retail water rate increases for FY 2025/26 through 2029/30; passed with Director Armitage the only no.

source.title: SCV Water Board approved minutes, April 1, 2025 (Resolution SCV-469 roll call)

bill-cooper.text: (2023) Moved, and voted for, Ordinance No. 03 raising directors' per-meeting compensation 6.7%, from $239 to $255; passed with Armitage, Colley and Petersen voting no.

source.title: SCV Water Board approved minutes, Dec. 19, 2023 (Ordinance No. 03 roll call)

bill-cooper.text: Campaign site: says SCV Water has "NO ability to approve or disprove" development and must by law supply water for it; warns that without planned growth "Young families would be forced to move outside of our community to afford housing."

source.title: Re-Elect Bill Cooper for SCV Water Board 2026 (campaign site)

bill-cooper.text: Campaign "myths" page: "SCV Water rates are some of the lowest in Southern California," about 37 cents per 100 gallons; says local water "meets or exceeds all state and federal requirements."

source.title: Bill Cooper campaign: SCV Water Agency Myths

bill-cooper.text: Writes that "climate change is changing the picture and is having a major effect on snowpack" and backs conservation rebates such as turf replacement and smart controllers.

noah-m-ropp.text: Pledges to vote "against rate increases to protect ratepayers' pocketbooks" and against "unnecessary expenditures like increases to board member stipends."

source.title: Ballotpedia: Noah Ropp (2026 Candidate Connection survey)

noah-m-ropp.text: Would continue and expand the Ratepayer Assistance Program so customers can afford bills "regardless of their situation," and make large industrial users fully pay for their demand.

source.title: Ballotpedia: Noah Ropp (2026 Candidate Connection survey)

noah-m-ropp.text: Wants more water-quality testing for perchlorate from the Whittaker-Bermite site, PFAS and microplastics, more frequent testing near Chiquita Canyon Landfill, and contaminant cleanup written into agency budget priorities.

source.title: Ballotpedia: Noah Ropp (2026 Candidate Connection survey)

noah-m-ropp.text: Supports expanding recycled water and stormwater capture, stricter water-efficiency rules for landscaping in new developments, and climate-focused committees to prepare for "the climate crisis actively harming our community."

source.title: Ballotpedia: Noah Ropp (2026 Candidate Connection survey)

noah-m-ropp.text: Describes himself as an environmental organizer who has fought "dirty fuel projects" and "electricity-guzzling data centers"; says no corporate money funds his campaign.

source.title: Ballotpedia: Noah Ropp (2026 Candidate Connection survey)

noah-m-ropp.text: Says government has a duty to ensure "the vulnerable receive the support they need" and that true equality of opportunity is achieved regardless of race or class.

source.title: Ballotpedia: Noah Ropp (2026 Candidate Connection survey)

noah-m-ropp.text: Endorsed by the Santa Clarita Valley Democrats, LA County Democratic Party, California Democratic Party, and SCV Water director Kathye Armitage.

notes: Cooper: board roll-call votes from SCV Water's own approved minutes, plus his campaign site (endorsements page is empty; no Ballotpedia survey). Ropp: Ballotpedia survey (mirrors his campaign issues page) and endorsements. Searches used: 9
